heading: INT. FERRY TERMINAL HOLDING ROOM - NIGHT COURT - NIGHT

units.text: INT. FERRY TERMINAL HOLDING ROOM - NIGHT COURT - NIGHT
A waiting hall that was once for passengers, now rigged as a courtroom with folding tables and a flag on a mic stand.
Salt damp climbs the tile.
Somewhere a ship's horn sounds and fades.
NNEKA ADEBAYO, 35, public defender, stands at the defense table with a coat she has not taken off.
She keeps one hand flat on a file as though it might fly.
Beside her, DEZ FAIRWEATHER, 22, in a paper jumpsuit, jiggles his knee.
He studies the ceiling tiles.
He does not look at her.
Across the aisle, ELLIOT VANCE, 40s, prosecutor, polishes his glasses on his tie.
He is smiling at nothing.
At the back, bailiff MORRIS KOWALSKI, 60, leans on a vending machine, eating something orange from a bag.
PRISCILLA TRAN, 25, the clerk, types with her whole face.
A speaker box on a pole CRACKLES.
Counsel, can you hear me? The river fog has closed the bridge. I'm appearing from the car.
units.name: JUDGE LAVOIE

units.text: We can hear you, Your Honor.
units.name: NNEKA

units.text: Good. Mr. Vance, the state's position on bail.
units.name: JUDGE LAVOIE

units.text: Vance stands.
He buttons his jacket, then unbuttons it, then sits back down, as if reconsidering the whole idea of standing.
The state has no objection to release, Your Honor.
units.name: ELLIOT

units.text: Nneka's head snaps toward him.
She searches his face for the joke.
No objection?
units.name: NNEKA

units.text: New evidence. The camera footage places the defendant at the Marlow Street shelter at the time of the break-in.
units.name: ELLIOT

units.text: That's what I told you.
units.name: DEZ

units.text: Nneka covers his hand with hers to quiet him.
She is already thinking three moves ahead and does not like where it leads.
Your Honor, the defense moves for dismissal.
units.name: NNEKA

units.text: Is the state opposed?
units.name: JUDGE LAVOIE

units.text: Vance hesitates.
He turns, very slightly, to the clerk.
Priscilla stops typing.
He tilts his head.
She shakes hers once, small, a flicker.
The state is... opposed. Your Honor. I've just been informed that the footage was timestamped from a different clock.
units.name: ELLIOT

units.text: Informed by whom?
units.name: NNEKA

units.text: Priscilla goes pale.
Morris looks up from his bag.
Ms. Adebay, sit down.
units.name: JUDGE LAVOIE

units.text: It's Adebayo, Your Honor, and I'd like the clerk to explain the clock.
units.name: NNEKA

units.text: The intercom hisses.
Dez rises half out of his chair.
Morris sets down the bag and walks forward, one hand drifting to his belt.
I didn't do it. I never did it. Why does it keep changing?
units.name: DEZ

units.text: He tries to say more and can't.
Nneka puts a hand on his shoulder and, for the first time, looks at him.
Sit. I've got you.
units.name: NNEKA

units.text: He sits.
She stands.
The fog presses at the windows like a face.
